context_documents.title: 2025-1771 · Wrist freedom creates L1 value and a collision-planning obligation
context_documents.body:
# 2025-1771: Wrist freedom creates L1 value and a collision-planning obligation

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The team explicitly credits 4414’s 2023 continuous elevator. Its carriage combines a pivot, wrist and compliant coral/algae end effector; range sensors and a transverse wheel actively center coral. The software models tested safe poses and allows only transitions connected in a graph.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The interview ties the wrist to effective L1 cycles and the pivot to serving both ground and station acquisition. The restricted transition graph is intended to prevent destructive arm/elevator interactions and overshoot.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The wrist should not be justified only by branch reach. It also changes how coral can be presented to the trough, so its value can rise in a low-task alliance role. The price is a larger configuration space: correct endpoint poses do not prove that the path between them is safe. A tested edge graph is a concrete way to carry mechanical clearance assumptions into software.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test every allowed transition under lag, sensor error and simultaneous chassis motion. Measure L1 throughput as well as L4 reach, and verify active centering before the final placement motion.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: 1771 North Gwinnett Robotics, Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.locator: Worlds interview, 1:23–3:29 lift and centering, 3:48–6:49 wrist, pivot and transitions, 7:06–8:59 reef-state controls
source_reviews.review_basis: Read on-page English transcript of the team interview
facts: Team describes a 4414-inspired continuous two-stage lift, separate carriage pivot and wrist, surgical-tube closure, two range sensors with a centering wheel, safe-state graph and a reef dashboard.
limitations: Auto-caption terms were interpreted in context. No video geometry, climb construction, or event-wide cycle statistics were established.

source_reviews.title: North Gwinnett Robotics team site
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the team’s named robot caption
facts: The team identifies the 2025 robot as Driftwood and describes it placing coral on the reef.
limitations: Caption confirms identity and task; no mechanical specification.

subsystems.name: Continuous elevator and dual-axis carriage
subsystems.construction: Two-stage continuous elevator inspired by 4414's 2023 lift, carrying a pivot and separate wrist.
subsystems.operation: The pivot alternates between floor handoff and station angles, including station approaches from either side. Wrist sets the L1 shelf angle.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team targeted quick L1 and all coral levels, floor and station supply, and shorter or less predictable approaches under defense.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: An additional axis can recover release geometry lost to short lift stroke. It also raises the number of intermediate poses that need clearance and overshoot testing.
subsystems.interfaces: Lift height controls cross-brace clearance. Pivot and wrist determine both the receiving pose at handoff and placement pitch at L1.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Recheck homing, mechanical stops and clearance on every allowed transition after a carriage impact or motor replacement.
subsystems.unknowns: Lift reeving, motors, reductions, mass and path coordinates.

subsystems.name: Shared roller claw and centering
subsystems.construction: Passive opening against surgical tubing, upper pull-in rollers, a transverse positioning wheel and two CANrange sensors.
subsystems.operation: Pull coral into the claw. Jog the tube toward dual detection, or deliberately shift it back for the L4 route. The claw can open around algae and retain it under elastic preload.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team wanted repeatable tube placement at release and explained that L4 needed an approach around the corner with its available lift height.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Two binary observations can define an acceptance window without estimating continuous tube position. Their overlap must survive range thresholds, tube skew and changing grip force.
subsystems.interfaces: Upper rollers accept both station feeds and floor handoff. The piece position couples directly to the collision margin at L4.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Look for stretched tubing, seized positioning rollers, and a sensor stuck on or off. Test a timeout or manual recovery if dual detection never occurs.
subsystems.unknowns: Roller diameters, tubing preload, sensor thresholds and exact L4 offset.

subsystems.name: Transition and reef-state controls
subsystems.construction: Allowed-state graph for the mechanism and a reef occupancy dashboard with operator entry and automatic tracking of robot actions.
subsystems.operation: The graph routes tested moves. The dashboard can mark coral placement and removed algae and use a selected goal to choose the next target.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team wanted to reduce target-selection time on short cycles and switch between ranking-point and playoff priorities.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Mechanical pose safety and scoring intent are separate state problems. A failed score or partner action can invalidate the dashboard even when the motion graph remains correct.
subsystems.interfaces: The target policy requests a pose and alignment, while the mechanism graph governs how the robot reaches it.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check behavior after an interrupted transition and after a failed score gets credited to occupancy. The interview included a dashboard restart, with no root cause given.
subsystems.unknowns: Fallback logic, position tolerances, homing recovery, and how driver overrides were implemented.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Driftwood packages a rotating pivot and wrist on the carriage of a continuous two-stage elevator. One spring-compliant roller claw receives from the floor collector or the human player station and handles algae as well as coral. The pivot provides station access from either side and swings the tool to the ground intake handoff. The wrist supplies a separate angle for a direct L1 shot. The team used horizontal movement of the tube within the claw as an extra clearance adjustment for L4, compensating for limited lift height.
source_review.piece_flow: Coral from either supply reaches the upper pull-in rollers on the claw. Two CANrange units are treated as binary presence detectors. When only one sees the tube, the centering wheel shifts it until both register. For L4 the team deliberately moves the tube back from its normal centered location to get around the branch geometry. For L1, the wrist aims to eject onto the trough shelf. Algae is held by the same compliant tool, and the team describes using the centering wheel for algae release as well. The transcript leaves the precise algae scoring pose and floor collector internals open.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Vertical carriage travel, carriage pivot and wrist rotation all change tool clearance. A pivot swing at the wrong height can put the tool or its arm into the elevator cross brace. The software uses a graph of tested states and permitted transitions. The two-sided station approach can eliminate a chassis turn if the robot reaches the station with the other end forward, but both paths have to end in the same usable piece registration.
revisions: Worlds interview documents the installed architecture as described there. No complete mechanism installation timeline was established.
transferable_principles: Design piece position as part of the tool pose. Build a graph from tested moves, and let the score policy select goals through that graph.
disconfirming_conditions: The benefit of a short lift and extra tool motions falls if repeatability at L4 degrades, dual detection is unreliable, or station access rarely rewards either-end approach.
remaining_gaps: Ground-intake construction and handoff tolerances, endgame hardware, drivetrain details and event-by-event chronology remain open.
recommended_images: Interview around 2:04–3:29 for candidate views of upper rollers, range sensors and shifted L4 piece position.
Interview around 7:54–8:44 for a candidate reef-state dashboard capture. Frame content requires separate inspection.
